# Reptar Framework: Canonical LLM & Agent Reference

Reptar is a high-performance, single-binary C# 13 web framework engineered for Native AOT and NetWasm (Cloudflare Workers). It features zero runtime reflection, compile-time validation, automatic OpenAPI / TypeScript codegen, native AI tool dispatch, and a lightweight typed query layer.

---

## 1. Machine-Readable Agent Commands & MCP Server

Before writing code or assuming database schema, query the framework's machine-readable state:

- `bun reptar inspect --json`: Complete project schema, active database dialect, tables, columns, indexes, routes, and migrations.
- `bun reptar doctor --json`: Diagnoses SDK toolchain (>= 10.0.401), Bun runtime, database connectivity, and RPC status.
- `bun reptar db plan --json`: Diffs C# `TableDef` schemas against the active database and returns planned SQL.
- `bun reptar db generate [--name <name>]`: Generates a timestamped `.sql` migration from planned changes.
- `bun reptar db migrate`: Applies all pending SQL migrations to the database.
- `bun reptar codegen`: Regenerates `@reptar/client` TypeScript RPC contracts from the C# route tree.
- `bun reptar mcp`: Launches the Model Context Protocol stdio server exposing `reptar_inspect`, `reptar_schema`, `reptar_routes`, `reptar_db_status`, `reptar_db_plan`, `reptar_check`, and `reptar_doctor`.

---

## 2. Defining Schemas and Typed Column Tokens

Reptar separates storage schema definitions (`TableDef`) from projection DTOs (`record`). Never use heavy attribute-laden records for DDL.

### Schema Definition (`schema/posts.cs`):
```csharp
using Reptar;
using static Reptar.ReptarApi;

public static partial class Schema
{
    public static readonly TableDef Posts = DefineTable("posts",
        Col.Text("id").PrimaryKey(),
        Col.Text("author_id").NotNull().Indexed(),
        Col.Text("slug").NotNull().Unique(),
        Col.Text("title").NotNull(),
        Col.Text("content").NotNull(),
        Col.Int("published").NotNull().Default(1),
        Col.Text("created_at").NotNull().DefaultSql("CURRENT_TIMESTAMP")
    );
    // ReptarTableGenerator automatically emits Schema.PostsCols.Id, Schema.PostsCols.Slug, etc.
    // (or directly Users.Email when the field is named `Table` on `public static partial class Users`).
}
```

### Projection DTO:
```csharp
[ReptarEntity("posts")]
public partial record PostDto(
    string Id,
    string AuthorId,
    string Slug,
    string Title,
    string Content,
    int Published,
    string CreatedAt
);
```

---

## 3. Querying the Database

### Type-Safe Filter Queries:
```csharp
// 1. List with filter, order by, and limit using Roslyn-generated ColumnRef<T> tokens
var activePosts = await ctx.Db.ListAsync<PostDto>(
    Schema.Posts,
    Schema.PostsCols.Published.Eq(1) & Schema.PostsCols.AuthorId.Eq(authorId),
    orderBy: Schema.PostsCols.CreatedAt.Desc(),
    limit: 20
);

// 2. Fluent TableQuery
var post = await ctx.Db.From<PostDto>(Schema.Posts)
    .Where(Schema.PostsCols.Slug.Eq("my-slug") & Schema.PostsCols.Published.Eq(1))
    .FirstOrDefaultAsync();

// 3. Count and Exists
var count = await ctx.Db.CountAsync(Schema.Posts, Schema.PostsCols.Published.Eq(1));
var exists = await ctx.Db.From<PostDto>(Schema.Posts)
    .Where(Schema.PostsCols.Slug.Eq("my-slug"))
    .ExistsAsync();

// 4. Delete Where
var deleted = await ctx.Db.DeleteWhereAsync(
    Schema.Posts,
    Schema.PostsCols.Id.Eq("post_123")
);
```

### Available ColumnRef Filter Methods:
- `.Eq(value)`, `.NotEq(value)`
- `.Gt(value)`, `.Gte(value)`, `.Lt(value)`, `.Lte(value)`
- `.Like(pattern)` (e.g. `"%word%"`)
- `.In(values)`, `.NotIn(values)`
- `.IsNull()`, `.IsNotNull()`
- Combinators: `filterA & filterB`, `filterA | filterB`, `!filter`
- OrderBy: `column.Asc()`, `column.Desc()`

### Raw SQL (First-Class Escape Hatch):
When complex joins or CTEs are required, raw SQL remains fully supported:
```csharp
var rows = await ctx.Db.QueryAsync<PostDto>(
    "SELECT p.* FROM posts p JOIN users u ON p.author_id = u.id WHERE u.email = @email ORDER BY p.created_at DESC LIMIT 20",
    ("email", userEmail)
);
```

---

## 4. Route Handlers & Validation

```csharp
var app = ReptarApp.Create();

// Synchronous JSON response
app.Get("/api/health", ctx => ctx.Json(new { ok = true, timestamp = DateTime.UtcNow }));

// Asynchronous handler with URL parameter (route params use the :name syntax)
app.Get("/api/posts/:slug", async ctx =>
{
    var slug = ctx.Req.Param("slug");
    var post = await ctx.Db.From<PostDto>(Schema.Posts)
        .Where(Schema.PostsCols.Slug.Eq(slug))
        .FirstOrDefaultAsync();

    return post is null
        ? ctx.NotFound("Post not found.")
        : ctx.Json(post);
});

// Validated POST request
var createPostValidator = ReptarApi.Rule<CreatePostInput>()
    .Prop(x => x.Title, r => r.NotNull().Min(3).Max(120))
    .Prop(x => x.Content, r => r.NotNull().Min(10));

app.Post("/api/posts", createPostValidator, async (ctx, input) =>
{
    var user = ctx.User!;
    var id = Guid.NewGuid().ToString("n");
    var slug = input.Title.ToLowerInvariant().Replace(' ', '-');

    await ctx.Db.InsertAsync(Schema.Posts, new
    {
        Id = id,
        AuthorId = user.Id,
        Slug = slug,
        Title = input.Title,
        Content = input.Content,
        Published = 1
    });

    return ctx.Json(new { id, slug }, 201);
}).AsAiTool("create_post", "Create and publish a new blog post");
```

---

## 5. AI Tool Bridge & LLM Streaming

Any Reptar route marked with `.AsAiTool(name, description)` automatically exports to OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini tool schemas without schema duplication:

```csharp
// Export tools as JSON schema:
app.MapAiTools("/api/ai/tools"); // Returns OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini compatible JSON

// In-process tool execution (no extra network hop):
var toolResult = await app.ExecuteAiToolAsync("create_post", argumentsJson, ctx);

// Token streaming with cancellation (stops LLM generation when client disconnects):
app.Post("/api/chat", async ctx =>
{
    IAsyncEnumerable<string> tokenStream = CallUpstreamLlmAsync(ctx.RequestAborted);
    return await ctx.StreamLlmAsync(tokenStream);
});
```

---

## 5b. Built-in Agent Engine (`Reptar.AI`, namespace `Reptar.AI`)

Reptar ships a provider-agnostic agent engine in the framework core (`framework/Reptar/AI/`): streaming LLM clients (OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, offline Echo), a ReAct loop, the standard workspace tools, SQLite session persistence, and the interactive terminal behind `bun reptar agent`.

### Mount workspace tools in one line

```csharp
using Reptar.AI;

app.UseWorkspaceTools(workspaceRoot: ".");   // read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_dir, run_command
```

Every tool is a normal Reptar route marked `.AsAiTool(...)` with path-traversal
protection against the workspace root, and dispatch happens **in-process** via
`app.ExecuteAiToolAsync` (zero HTTP overhead, full `Rule<T>` validation).

### Run the streaming agent loop

```csharp
var client = LlmClientFactory.FromEnvironment();       // OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Ollama/Echo
var history = new List<ChatMessage> { new("user", "fix the failing test") };

var summary = await StreamingAgentHarness.RunAsync(
    app, client, history,
    systemPrompt: "You are a coding agent in this repo.",
    maxSteps: 24,
    onEvent: evt =>
    {
        switch (evt)
        {
            case AgentEvent.TextDelta delta: Console.Write(delta.Text); break;
            case AgentEvent.ToolCallStarted call: Console.WriteLine($"→ {call.Name}"); break;
            case AgentEvent.ToolCallFinished call: Console.WriteLine($"{(call.Success ? "✓" : "✗")} {call.Name} {call.ElapsedMs:0}ms"); break;
        }
    });
// summary.StopReason / FinalContent / StepsTaken / ToolCallsExecuted / ElapsedMs
```

### Provider selection & credentials

`LlmConfig.FromEnvironment()` resolves in this order: explicit flags →
`REPTAR_AGENT_MODEL` / `REPTAR_AGENT_PROVIDER` / `REPTAR_AGENT_BASE_URL` →
first present key among `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` /
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` / `OLLAMA_HOST` →
credentials saved by `/connect` in `~/.reptar/agent/auth.json` (flat map,
`0600`, override the path with `REPTAR_AGENT_AUTH`) → offline `Echo` provider.

Interactive connection (pi `/login`, opencode `/connect` parity):
`bun reptar agent --connect [provider]` or `/connect` in-session — provider
picker with per-row status, hidden API-key entry, base URL override, live
connection test via `LlmCatalog.ListAsync` (models endpoint per provider),
model pick, then save + switch. `/providers` shows the status table
(source: env var or saved), `/models` picks from the live catalog,
`/disconnect` removes saved credentials. `Other` registers a custom
OpenAI-compatible endpoint (id + base URL + key + model); custom ids are
resolvable everywhere afterwards (`/model myid/model`, `--model myid/model`).

Registry: `LlmProviders.Known` (openai, anthropic, gemini, ollama, openrouter,
gateway) with env keys, default base URLs, and default models; custom
providers extend it through the auth file.

### Session persistence (AOT-safe)

```csharp
using Reptar.AI;

var store = new AgentSessionStore(
    app.Db,
    AgentSchema.Sessions("agent_sessions"),   // id PK, title, created_at
    AgentSchema.Messages("agent_messages"));   // id PK, session_id indexed, role, content, tool_calls, created_at
await store.EnsureCreatedAsync();
var session = await store.CreateSessionAsync("first chat");
await store.AppendMessageAsync(session.Id, new ChatMessage("user", "hello"));
var messages = await store.LoadMessagesAsync(session.Id);   // List<ChatMessage>
```

Row mapping is registered manually (zero reflection — no source generator
dependency for Native AOT apps).

### CLI

- `bun reptar agent` — interactive terminal agent in the current workspace
  (slash commands: `/reset /history /tools /model /sessions /session /new /exit`).
- `bun reptar agent --web [port]` — web companion on 4040 (`POST /api/chat` SSE, `GET /api/sessions`).
- `bun reptar agent --self-test` — 7-check offline verification of the tool bridge.
- `bun reptar run <app.cs>` — run any file-based app.

Reference app: `examples/agent-cli/` (see `plans/agent-engine.md` for the
full build report and AOT findings).

### Native AOT rule (critical)

Under Native AOT, `ctx.Json(new { ... })` and `ctx.Json(record)` serialize via
reflection and **fail at runtime** (`SmallObjectWithParameterizedConverter`).
In AOT-published code paths, build `JsonObject`/`JsonArray` and return
`ctx.JsonRaw(obj.ToJsonString())` instead.

---

## 6. Strict Agent Conventions

1. **Check Before Assuming**: Always run `bun reptar inspect --json` or use `reptar_schema` to verify existing tables, columns, and routes.
2. **Never Use Runtime Reflection**: Keep everything Native AOT and NetWasm compliant.
3. **No Attribute Salad DDL**: Do not attach `[PrimaryKey]` or `[Unique]` attributes to DTO records. Use `TableDef` in `schema/`.
4. **Always Use ColumnRef Over Strings**: Avoid `ctx.Db.ListAsync<T>(table, "where col = @val")` when `table.Col<T>("col").Eq(...)` is available.
5. **Keep Raw SQL Available**: Never remove raw SQL escape hatches (`QueryAsync`, `ExecuteAsync`).
